title: Common Problems
markdown:
| Problem | Usual cause | What to do | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disassembly is nonsense after a certain point | data inside code (a jump table, padding) decoded as instructions, or decoding started mid-instruction | find where real code resumes; mark the data as data; use recursive descent | 5.02 |
| A function you wrote is missing from the binary | inlined by the optimiser | look in its callers; compare with a Debug build | 1.02 |
| Addresses from yesterday no longer match | ASLR moved the module | record and use `module+offset` | 3.02 |
| Addresses from the old build no longer match | the program was rebuilt | use byte patterns with wildcards | 4.05 |
| A breakpoint never hits | the code runs in another thread, another module copy, or before you attached | break on module load; start the program under the debugger | 3.01 |
| Memory shows `CC` where code should be | your own software breakpoint, seen through a raw read | read through the debugger, which hides them | 3.01 |
| A scan finds thousands of results | wrong type or alignment, or too few narrowing scans | change the value and rescan; try float; scan aligned only | 3.03 |
| The value is found but resets every run | it lives on the heap | find what writes it, the object base, then a pointer path | 3.03 |
| A patched program crashes immediately | a patch overwrote part of the next instruction | patch whole instructions, pad with nops | 4.01 |
| A detour crashes in the cave | a stolen relative instruction was copied unchanged, or registers and flags were not preserved | relocate or refuse relative instructions; save state | 4.03 |
| A hook works for some calls but not others | an IAT hook only covers the module whose table changed | hook other modules' tables, or use an inline hook | 4.04 |
| A pattern matches many places | not distinctive enough | add instructions until it is unique | 4.05 |
| The PDB is refused | GUID or age does not match this build | find the PDB from the exact build; use a symbol server | 5.04 |
| `ReadProcessMemory` fails with error 299 | the region was freed or is not fully readable | re-query the map; read only committed readable regions | 5.03 |
| A section has entropy near 8 and few imports | the program is packed | analyse the unpacked code in memory, in a lab if it is not yours | 1.05 |
| A file format has bytes that change on every save | timestamps, counters or a checksum | take two saves with no change to separate them | 6.02 |
